ACIDSPRAY01: A store-bought Bug Kill EX Alpha spray picked up by a squad leader. It is of little use as a weapon. Lab modifications made it just strong enough to slow enemies down.
ENERGY_LASERLANCE101: The final Laser Lance upgrade. Its extraordinary power once kept it off the battlefield. It consumes a great deal of energy to achieve the longest range of any lance, with high destructive power.
ENERGY_LIGHTNINGSNIPER11: Pale Wing's ultimate weapon. Its discharge is so powerful that the barrel and plasma E-unit must enter emergency cooling. The unit is unavailable until cooling and recharging are complete.
ENERGY_PRASMACANNON101: The ultimate RSR Plasma Launcher. Its power was once considered too great for deployment. Both destructive power and blast radius have been greatly increased.
ENERGY_PRASMAGRENADE400: The final Plasma Grenade F upgrade. Increased power and a wider blast make it even more dangerous. A skilled user can put that power to good use.
ENERGY_RIFLE403EMP: An electromagnetic pulse weapon and the final Pulsar Shot upgrade. A built-in plasma generator reduces energy use and increases output, range, damage, and projectile count. It has no effect on living creatures.
GRENADE03: A hand grenade with enormous destructive power. Its heavy charge makes it hard to throw far. It was found sealed in a storehouse marked Danger. The impact fuse detonates on contact after it is thrown.
GRENADE406: A grenade with tremendous destructive power. It detonates four seconds after being thrown. Timed fuse.
MISSILELAUNCHER13: The final Emerald launcher upgrade, with higher damage and a wider blast. This ultimate missile system was kept secret in the EDF lab.
MISSILELAUNCHER14: The final Prominence launcher upgrade. Its large missile travels straight at first, then starts homing sharply. Its destructive power kept it off the battlefield until now.
REPAIRSPRAY015: Launches a capsule that bursts on impact, spreading repair nanomachines. It reaches farther than a Reverser and restores vehicle durability or troop armor. Limited nanomachines mean it cannot be reloaded.
REPAIRSPRAY045: An upgraded Reverse Shooter. Capsules spread more nanomachines across a wider area, restoring more armor at the cost of greatly reduced range. It also heals the user and cannot be reloaded.
REPAIRSPRAY400: Sprays nanomachines that harden into invisible armor. They repair vehicle durability and troop armor. To limit exposure, the device is configured to have no effect on its user. It cannot be reloaded.
REPAIRSPRAY407: The final Aerial Reverser. It creates a huge healing cloud that also affects the user. Its area is large enough for enemies to benefit, so use it carefully. It cannot be reloaded.
REPAIRSPRAY436: Fires capsules that burst on impact and spread repair nanomachines across a wide area. It reaches farther than a Reverser, affects the user, and cannot be reloaded.
REPAIRSPRAY437: The final Reverse Shooter. A huge blast scatters repair nanomachines over a wide area. Transport in capsules is safe, so it can heal its user as well. It cannot be reloaded.
RIFLEA03: A D model that trades rate of fire for heavier hits. It deals substantially more damage than earlier D models, at the cost of accuracy.
RIFLEA07: A special AS-99D modification that sacrifices fire rate to maximize the power of each shot. It also has a long effective range.
RIFLER07: An upgraded AS-99 RR model. It fires much faster than an R model and hits far harder than the AS-22RR.
ROCKETLAUNCHER105: A superweapon based on the Goliath-99 that surpasses its destructive power. Its origins are unknown. It is beyond what human science was thought capable of developing.
SHOTGUN100: An exceptionally powerful shotgun once thought beyond human technology. The circumstances of its development remain classified.
SHOTGUN11: A specially modified SG-99 with even greater destructive power. Only selected soldiers are issued this weapon.
SHOTGUN12: The ultimate Sparrow Shot. Designed for rapid fire, it combines tremendous destructive power with an excellent firing rate. Its existence is a top EDF secret.
